reason: I want to follow glucose across the intestinal lining toward the liver, matching the first goal.
expectation: I expect glucose to cross the villus into its blood vessels, though the next stage of the route is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Following fat is also relevant, but I chose to start with the glucose route.

reaction: The picture makes the crossing clear, though the result was expected.
reason: Amino acids share the goal of reaching the liver, so I want to follow their route next.
expectation: I expect amino acids to cross the intestinal lining into villus blood, as glucose did.

alternatives.reason: I considered following fat next, but want to complete the two routes grouped in the first goal.

effect: Amino acids also entered a villus blood capillary, as expected.
reaction: The parallel with glucose is clear, though predictable.
reason: Combining the two blood-borne products may advance their shared route toward the liver.
expectation: I expect glucose and amino acids to be grouped for transport toward the liver; the precise next step is unclear.

alternatives.reason: I considered following fat next, but want to advance the shared blood route first.

effect: Glucose and amino acids now travel together in blood toward the liver, completing their goal.
reaction: The result clearly connects the villus capillaries to the liver.
reason: The remaining goal concerns fat, so I want to follow its digestion products across the villus.
expectation: I expect the fat digestion products to enter intestinal cells, where they can be packaged for transport.

alternatives.reason: Packaging materials seem relevant, but I want to bring the fat into the villus first.

effect: The fat digestion products entered intestinal cells, ready for the packaging step.
reaction: The crossing was clear and matched my expectation.
reason: Packaging the fat should advance the remaining goal of sending it into lymph.
expectation: I expect the intestinal cells to package the fat into lipoprotein particles that can enter lymph.

alternatives.reason: The lacteal entrance will likely be needed for the lymph route, but packaging seems to come first.

effect: The fat was rebuilt and packaged into chylomicrons inside the intestinal cells, ready for the lymph route.
reaction: The explanation makes the packaging step clearer and introduces a useful name for the particles.
reason: The lacteal is the villus's lymph vessel, so combining its entrance with the chylomicrons should advance the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the chylomicrons to enter the lacteal and travel into lymph.

effect: Chylomicrons entered the villus lymph vessel, completing the fat route and showing that lymph carries them onward to the blood.
reaction: The final explanation made the difference between the fat and blood routes clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Packaging fat into chylomicrons was the most worthwhile action: it explained what intestinal cells do before fat enters lymph.

leastWorthwhile.text: Following glucose and amino acids separately felt somewhat repetitive because their crossings had parallel results.

surprise.text: I learned that intestinal cells rebuild fat and package it into chylomicrons before it enters lymph.

arbitrary.text: Combining glucose and amino acids already in villus blood felt a little artificial, although the result clearly explained their shared route toward the liver.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see how the absorbed nutrients are used, though the predictable sequence of compatible choices limits the gameplay interest.
